title: Normalized strict integral model at one coefficient field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, and $f:Z\to X$ a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. There exists an IntegralModel over $E$ [def-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-data]: its strict reduction diagram, ambient universal-unit identification, actual-augmentation reconstruction normalization, additive and scalar-linear integral image, scalar equation and native reconstruction shift compatibility are all retained. This statement involves one field only, and asserts no comparisons between different fields or rationalizations.

source.place: Agent-expanded strict scalar comparison argument, original DAG Steps 1--8; current blueprint retains only the underlying closed-immersion argument.

proof.text: The finite-type schemes $Z,X$ are Noetherian: choose finite affine covers by finite-type $k$-algebras and apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a field has only two ideals). They are finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and $\ell$ remains invertible under their structural ring maps. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] applies. By [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible], the specified $I_E$ has values in $\mathcal C_E(X)$. The normalized comparison [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison], interpreted on strict diagrams as required by [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], gives the actual natural isomorphism $\psi_E:F_E\to I_E$, not merely isomorphic values. Consequently $F_E$ also preserves these full constructible subcategories. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible], each specified $S^W_{L/E}$ preserves them too.

source.place: Rational-stage paragraph and algebraically closed-stage scalar comparison; returned proof steps 4-5 (comparison normalization), 8 (linearity) and 9 first paragraph (comparison transport and coherence)

proof.text: The ambient $F_E$ is additive and $R_E$-linear by [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]. With the constant-section action of [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear], naturality gives $I_E(h)=\psi_{E,V}F_E(h)\psi_{E,U}^{-1}$. Bilinearity of composition therefore gives $I_E(ah)=aI_E(h)$ and $I_E(h+h')=I_E(h)+I_E(h')$. Taking $h=\operatorname{id}$ in naturality yields $I_E(a\operatorname{id}_K)\psi_{E,K}=\psi_{E,K}F_E(a\operatorname{id}_K)$; these are precisely the constant scalar multiplications. In particular the normalized comparison itself respects them.

proof.text: We check shifts for $\psi_E$ with the specified, rather than transported, shifts. Its construction in [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] is $F_E$ of the strict reduction augmentation followed by the strict-tower direct-image/limit comparison and the coefficient-restriction comparisons of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. The augmentation has quotient maps in the unshifted product coordinate and zero in the shifted coordinate by [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model]. Under a shift by $r$, its first coordinate is simply reindexed and its zero coordinate remains zero; the signed Roos shift therefore commutes with it by [lem-weil-roos-comm-shift]. For the remaining comparisons use their K-injective derived-composition normalization [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]: on $I$ and a resolution $j:f_*I\to J$ the comparison is represented by $g_*j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], $I[r],J[r],j[r]$ are permissible shifted resolutions; the comparison is then $g_*(j[r])=(g_*j)[r]$. This is an equality of chain maps, hence of the entire derived comparisons. Applied also to the tower-site factorizations, it proves shift compatibility of all factors of $\psi_E$. This argument uses the normalized strict-derived-limit comparison, not uniqueness from evaluated projections.
